posts.post_subject: Is Display holography dying or Morphing into something new?
posts.content_md:
I do believe their will always be a few who love the art of holography and have home built labs. But it seem as a whole display holography is either sleeping or dying a slow death or going thru another cycle. Or has everything been tried? Also with the cost of everything going up there are a few looking into making their own plates. So it can’t be too dead.

 Even in this forum I remember the days when the activity on this forum was hot and cutting edge. Now there are only a hand full that post, but yet there are a lot that read the information posted on the forum. Which would give the idea that it is not obsolete. 

Also with the cost of everything going up there are a few looking into making their own plates. 

I do believe Colins HoloWiki is keeping some of the basic info for future Holographers is a good thing.

What can we do? 

If it’s asleep what can we do to wake it up? 

Or what can we do to make this forum alive again? 

Any ideas?

posts.author: Dutchelm05
posts.post_subject: Is Display holography dying or Morphing into something new?
posts.content_md:
This is a great topic Danny.

Here is my two cents:

I would like to see a list of the great (and not so great) unanswered questions in holography (for me especially in DCG). I have read many old threads which start off great but then peter out. This might encourage people like myself to take on one or two experiments during the coarse of a normal shoot. It also allows mentoring and guidance from the forum gurus. Then IMO results should be collaborated, then placed into Wiki.

The only problem I see is there is only a hand full of us who post (in the DCG section). Hundreds seem to read but do not add anything to the conversation. Years past, there were maybe a dozen or so DCG types, now maybe half that. And with the absence of the greats like Jeff and Martin (and others) who operate in the higher theoretical realm we lose a dimension of viability. Good or bad, the hand full of us that are here need to establish the grassroots movement. Show progress and hope others will start coming back, or new folks come around. Set aside any past differences and start showing results.

As to John's point on a water cooler section, anything that promotes teamwork and humanizes the good folks on the forum is a big plus. I would perfer tips on how to keep the wife happy so she doesn't mind another 2:00 in the morning lab run. Tip #1 during the dark reaction time, rub her feet, and don't set your timer so it beeps after 5 minutes (a real mood breaker)

posts.content_md:
> **Danny Bee:** maybe we have a 2008 or 2009 PCG meeting in calif

Well that would be great.

The way I see it (IMHO) we have like 5 serious DCG'ers (who post) John, Dave, Danny, Joe and myself. It would be great if we all collectively decided to take on a project of some importance. Not impossible but something we can all feel proud of at the end and use when we do shoot. Perhaps consulting Jeff and Martin (and anyone else) would be helpful to see if they are interested. Then see if as a group, we can actually do it, or at least see where we are struggling at. I'm not big at some grand unifying idea but I do think showing some results by working together would be a big step.

If the group think it best, we can include other types of holographers, the more the better, but also complex. I'm cool with anything. 

I have said it before in that I have worked with all of the DCG'ers and the experience has been great. I think it is possible to do something really good and worth wide.

Just my opinion
